cases.name: the behavior catalog > lists every behavior the engine runs, to any caller, and describes one by name

data.name: Approvals
data.description: Sign-offs that gate states of the type's Workflow. A transition into a gated state, from a state its gate allows, waits until as many distinct principals holding the gate's permission as its count have signed off; the instance's creator cannot sign unless the gate allows it. A change of the instance's own fields consumes every gate's sign-offs, unless the config keeps them, and entering a gated state consumes that gate's, so a return to it signs again. Consumed sign-offs stay listed. Deleting the instance deletes its sign-offs.

data.name: Branches
data.description: Makes each instance the root of a version graph: refs, a primary line and drafts of it, over rows of the kinds the config names, each kind's content a type of the schema document; commits, merges, rebases and reverts; and a release pointer whose history is the release log, its version the release field. The instance's own fields stay outside the graph. The graph lives in the behavior's own tables, and deleting the instance deletes it. With sweep in its config, a schedule discards idle drafts and keeps the graph's storage in bounds.

data.name: Comments
data.description: A conversation on the instance: messages, each top-level or a reply in the thread of a top-level one, one level deep, which their authors edit and delete, others react to and pin, and whose threads are resolved and reopened. A message may be streamed as it is written: begin holds its place as composing, appendDraft adds to its draft and sends the draft signal to the streams open on the instance, and finish posts it; one whose author stops appending for composeTimeoutMs is interrupted, keeping what was written. Readers send typing and viewing, signals the engine delivers and does not keep. Each caller has a read marker on the conversation and on each thread, which markRead moves, and follows the threads it posts in, is mentioned in, or follows with follow. Each message that comes to stand, and each edit that adds a mention, records a delivery for each subject it mentions and each follower of its thread but its author, which a notifier or an agent dispatcher outside the engine claims and settles with claimDeliveries and settleDeliveries; the engine sends nothing. inbox reads a caller's mentions, followed threads and read conversations across every schema of the namespace it may read, and searchMessages searches the bodies of the messages that stand. A message written by an agent or a service acting for someone records that subject as for: the subject follows its thread and hears of it from no delivery, as its author does, while its author, the caller, is the one whose read markers, follows, reactions and drafts it writes; acting for someone grants nothing an author or a permission holder may do. Besides ref and action blocks, a message may hold code blocks, a place in code at a revision with the text captured when it was posted, which moveAnchor moves to the same code at a newer revision, and attachment blocks, the description of a file the deployment stores. Every writing operation on an instance is beside the instance: it writes Comments' own tables, never moves the instance's seq, ETag or updatedAt, and runs none of its guards, so a lease on the instance does not stop a reply. A caller who may read the instance reads the conversation; the policy is asked write for a writing operation, post included. Deleting the instance deletes its conversation, with its read markers, follows, deliveries and search index.

data.name: Constants
data.description: Fields of the type that its create sets and nothing changes after: an update that changes one, a caller's or one a behavior's operation applies, is refused at the field, unless the caller holds the config's permission. A field the create leaves absent stays absent. What routes an instance, such as a step's kind or the key a blueprint stamped it with, stays what its create gave it.

data.name: Dependencies
data.description: Blockers between instances. A blocker is finished once its status is a terminal state of its own schema's Workflow whose outcome the config accepts, a success by default. An instance is blocked while a blocker is not finished, and a transition of its own Workflow into a gated state waits until none blocks it. A blocker is an instance of the type's own schema, or of a schema the config lists, that composes Workflow; an edge that would close a cycle is refused. A create may give its blockers. Deleting a blocker removes its edges.

data.name: Derived
data.description: Own fields a model outside the engine fills from other own fields, under an instruction the schema holds (D73). The engine calls no model: a deriver holding the config's permission pulls the stale fields with staleDerivations (each one's inputs, instruction, model label and the field's JSON Schema, which is the output's) and settles its answers with settleDerivations, presenting the hash it pulled. A value is written with the operation's update(), so the type's validation and every guard judge it, and its event attributes it to Derived with the confidence given. A field is stale when its inputs, instruction, model or type moved since its last value; that value stays until a new one settles. Once a caller, or another behavior's operation, writes a derived field, Derived stops deriving it until rederive. A failure appends no event; after maxAttempts the field waits until its inputs move. Deleting the instance deletes what Derived keeps of it.

data.name: Links
data.description: Named links from the instance to instances of the schemas its config names, set by link or given at create: each holds one target, or with many a list of them. A pinned link records the target's revision (its schema composes Revisions) or its release (its schema composes Branches), and reports the target's latest beside it and whether the target has moved past it. A required link is given at create, can be moved to another target but not unlinked, and the delete of its target is refused; a required many-valued link keeps at least one target, and only its last target's delete is refused. A deleted target leaves every link that holds it.

data.name: Numbering
data.description: A number a person reads on each instance, set in its create's transaction from a count per namespace and schema: the format prints it, INV-{yyyy}-{seq:4} as INV-2026-0042. The count may run per target of a required, single-valued link and start again each UTC year, so a label is unique within its scope. A refused create takes no number; a delete leaves a gap. Nothing changes a number once set, and a list finds an instance by its label or its number. An instance made before its schema composed Numbering is numbered by assignNumber.

data.name: Provenance
data.description: Who set each own field last, and through what (D73): a caller's create or update, or the behavior whose operation wrote it, with the confidence that operation attributed (D16, amended). With review, a write from the sources it names is proposed until a reviewer holding its permission accepts or rejects it, unless its confidence reaches below; a caller's write over a proposal makes it edited. A gate refuses a move of the type's Workflow into its state while a field it lists is proposed. Deleting the instance deletes its records.

data.name: Reactions
data.description: Rules that move Workflow statuses after a change commits: when the instance's status enters a state, when a field of the instance, its own or a behavior's, changes, when every instance that links to it through a link is in a terminal state, optionally one with a listed outcome, when one of them enters a terminal state with a listed outcome, when an all or any rollup of the instance comes to hold, or when the instance one of its links points to gains a revision or a release, move the instance, or the instance one of its links points to, to a state. An engine runs them after the commit, as the principal it names for its runner, so a rule never refuses the change that set it off. A target already in the state, with no transition to it, or whose guards refuse is left as it is.

data.name: Revisions
data.description: Immutable revisions of the instance's own fields: one when it is created and one each time they change, numbered 1, 2, 3, ..., read a page at a time or one by its number. With review in its config, a caller can propose a change as a merge patch, citing instances as evidence, and a caller who holds the review permission approves it, which applies the patch as an update, or rejects it; pendingProposals counts the proposals waiting. Deleting the instance deletes its revisions and proposals.

data.name: Rollups
data.description: Values derived from the instances that point at this one through a link of their schema's Links config: how many there are, how many hold each value of a field, the sum, least or greatest of a numeric field, a field's value on the one created last, and whether every one or some one is in a terminal state of its schema's Workflow, optionally one with a listed outcome. A value is computed when the instance is read, as the caller, from at most 500 linked instances; a rollup over more has none. A rollup of every or some one may gate states of the type's Workflow: a transition into one waits until the rollup holds.

data.name: Search
data.description: Full-text search over the instance's own text fields, which the config names, and with vectors in the config, vector search over embeddings an outside embedder computes from the same text. The index is kept in the transaction of each create, update and delete; an embedder pulls the instances whose text changed since their vector was computed (staleEmbeddings) and settles their vectors back (settleEmbeddings). The schema-level search returns the matching ids in rank order, by the text, by a vector the caller gives, or by both fused, from the instances of the caller's namespace only, and similar returns the instances nearest to one, or to a draft's text.

data.name: StateRules
data.description: Rules per state of the type's Workflow: the own fields an instance must hold to enter a state, and the ones that cannot change while it is in it. A field is held when it is neither absent nor null. A transition into a state while a field it requires is not held is vetoed, and a create whose initial state requires one is refused at the field. An update, a caller's or one a behavior's operation applies, that clears a field the instance's state requires, or changes one it freezes, is vetoed; a caller with the config's permission may change a frozen field. Requires Workflow.

data.name: Timers
data.description: Named deadlines on the instance, each due a time after it starts: at the create, each time the status of the type's Workflow enters a state, or at the time a date-time field of the instance holds, before it with a negative offset. A due deadline fires once: it is marked fired and can move the status, from the state it starts in unless the config names others, whatever the move meets. A change of the status can cancel a pending deadline, and a field deadline moves with its field. The engine's runner fires the due deadlines every sweepMs; a caller with the config's permission resets or snoozes one. A deadline that names a state needs Workflow on the type.

data.name: Variants
data.description: Types an open JSON field of the type by the value of another of its fields: while by holds a value types lists, field, when it holds a value, is held to that type of the schema document as a field of the type is, unknown keys refused at every depth; while by holds another value or none, field holds none. A result whose shape differs per kind of step is refused when it is written in the wrong shape. The describe document and the create and update tools show each variant.

data.name: Workflow
data.description: A state machine on the instance: a status that starts in the initial state and changes only through transition, along a transition the config lists. A transition may name a permission the caller must hold. A state that no transition leaves is terminal, and a terminal state has an outcome: success, failure or neutral, success unless the config says otherwise. Other instances' blockers, rollups and reactions read it.

data.name: test.Counter
data.description: Counts up from a start, to an optional limit.

data.name: test.Flag
data.description: Holds an instance still while it is flagged.

data.name: test.Tally
data.description: Counts the updates of an instance and bumps its counter.
